proof_summary: Factoring factorials into their divisible and unit parts expresses the successive binomial ratios through products \(\beta_t=\prod_{p\nmid k}(1+t p^r/k)\), while doubling and reflection symmetries of the units modulo \(p^r\) yield strong valuations for the reciprocal power sums. A quartic Newton expansion approximates each \(\beta_t\) to valuation \(5r-1\), and the reflection identities cancel the low-order terms in \(F(2)-3F(1)+2\); together with auxiliary Wolstenholme-type bounds for the preceding binomial coefficients, this supplies the required valuation.
